e2be825e0d.what_happened: Donald Trump is scheduled to headline his third cryptocurrency gala on Sunday night at his Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia, rewarding top holders of his $TRUMP meme coin. The event includes meet-and-greets with Floyd Mayweather, Kevin O’Leary, Tristan Thompson and Lior Suchard, and perks are divided by tiers for 185 holders. Democrats accuse Trump of improperly profiting from his crypto ventures and have vowed to investigate conflicts of interest and push legislation banning such activities.
details: Trump is set to headline his third crypto gala on Sunday night at Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia. The event rewards top holders of his $TRUMP meme coin and includes meet-and-greets with Floyd Mayweather, Kevin O’Leary, Tristan Thompson and Lior Suchard, according to its website. Access is split by tiers for 185 holders: 120 attendees get a Trump fragrance, poster, “commemorative” ticket and “Trump watch”; the top 29 get a VIP reception; the top four get a “TRUMP 18K Gold Watch.”

Democrats say Trump is improperly profiting from his crypto ventures and have criticized him and his family for monetizing his brand through equities and crypto while he is in office. After sweeping wins in the midterms, Democrats vowed to investigate conflicts of interest involving Trump and his personal wealth during his presidency and to push for legislation banning activities such as the meme coin gala dinner. Last month, Adam Schiff and eight other US senators sent a letter saying the dinner and scoring system appeared built to increase investment in $TRUMP and let the president abuse his office to enrich himself.

Since returning to the White House, Trump has made more than $1bn from his crypto businesses, according to financial disclosures released in June. He received more than $500m from World Liberty Financial selling new crypto products and another $600m from sales of souvenir-type “meme” coins stamped with his face; he launched the $Trump meme coin days before his inauguration. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while White House spokesperson Anna Kelly told Reuters earlier this year that neither the president nor his family has ever engaged or will ever engage in conflicts of interest and that Trump proudly made the United States the crypto capital of the world through executive actions.

Interest in the $TRUMP dinner has fallen, with contestants’ combined holdings dropping from $148m in May 2025 to $8.6m in this month’s gala; an analysis of blockchain data for Reuters by Public Citizen found more than half of the digital wallets publicly listed on the contest leaderboard for Sunday’s dinner are tied directly to crypto exchanges that bar US-based users, indicating links to foreign nationals. The Trump family’s other crypto-connected equities and ventures have fallen to record lows, and outside investors in their five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5bn, according to a Reuters analysis. The meme coin has earned the Trump family at least $635m, according to the president’s June financial disclosure statement; in total, the Trumps had earned at least $2.3bn through April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin, and the president’s stake in a fifth crypto-linked venture, Trump Media & Technology Group, is worth about $430m.
e2be825e0d.why_it_matters: Democrats say the gala lets Trump use his office to enrich himself and have vowed investigations and legislation to ban such activities.

3663428557.what_happened: WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called for peace after heavy fighting near a hospital in Ituri province disrupted Ebola response efforts. The fighting had been ongoing since yesterday close to where the Ebola outbreak first emerged, forcing health workers and aid partners to shelter in a maternity ward for more than 24 hours. As of November 17, the DRC had 11,613 Ebola cases and 5,678 deaths in its largest and deadliest outbreak.
details: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus spoke on Sunday about heavy fighting near a hospital in Ituri province. The fighting had been ongoing since yesterday in an area close to where the Ebola outbreak first emerged. It disrupted Ebola response efforts and forced health workers and aid partners to shelter inside a maternity ward for more than 24 hours.

Tedros said the situation puts patients, families and health workers at grave risk. As of November 17, the WHO reported 11,613 Ebola cases and 5,678 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. This is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country.

Ituri and North Kivu in eastern DRC remain the most affected provinces. The WHO said on Saturday that while some areas saw a slight decline in cases, sustained high-level transmission continues overall. The virus spreads through contact with bodily fluids and has spread across the DRC's east and northeast, areas plagued by violence for more than 30 years.

Earlier in November, armed men thought to be linked to an ISIL (ISIS)-affiliated group raided villages in North Kivu and killed dozens of people, forcing patients with confirmed and suspected Ebola infections to flee. The outbreak is also happening amid fighting between government forces and the Rwanda-backed M23 armed group, which has seized key cities in eastern DRC. This makes transport of healthcare resources to remote regions difficult, and the WHO is working to arrange a safe exit for the team and to protect hospital facilities, staff and patients.

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on Sunday that battle disrupted Ebola response work and forced medical staff and aid partners to shelter inside a maternity ward for more than a day. As of November seventeenth, country has recorded eleven thousand six hundred thirteen cases and five thousand six hundred seventy eight deaths in its largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak. The virus spreads through bodily fluids, and eastern provinces like Ituri and North Kivu remain the hardest hit. The region has faced violence for over thirty years, and fighting between government forces and a Rwanda-backed group is making it hard to move medical supplies. 2056756415.what_happened: Two fishermen died and a third person was badly hurt after a train hit them in the Cod Bay Fisheries Harbour area of Trincomalee on the night of the 22nd. The three were standing on the railway track when a train going from Trincomalee to Colombo Fort struck them. One died at the scene and another later died in hospital.
details: Police said three people were standing on the railway track when a train travelling from Trincomalee to Colombo Fort hit them in the Cod Bay Fisheries Harbour area of Trincomalee on the night of the 22nd. One person died right at the spot.
The other two were taken to Trincomalee Hospital with serious injuries. One of them later died while being treated, bringing the death toll to two.
The two dead men were both fishermen, aged 48 and 58, from the Matara and Dondra areas. Their bodies were placed at the Trincomalee Hospital mortuary.
The China Bay Police are looking further into what happened.

2056756415.spoken: Here's a sad story from Trincomalee. On the night of the twenty-second, three people were standing on a railway track near the Cod Bay Fisheries Harbour when a train came through. Police say the train was heading from Trincomalee to Colombo Fort, and it struck all three of them. One person died right there at the scene. The other two were rushed to Trincomalee Hospital with serious injuries, but sadly one of them also died while being treated. The two who lost their lives were both fishermen, aged forty-eight and fifty-eight, and they came from the Matara and Dondra areas. Their bodies have been kept at the hospital mortuary. The China Bay Police are now investigating exactly how this happened.

fce8bbdea9.what_happened: Environment Minister Dammika Patabendi denied saying that elephant Kawanthissa died from diarrhoea. He said a daily Sri Lankan Sinhala-language newspaper report was inaccurate. He stressed that only a post-mortem report can determine the real cause of death.
details: Environment Minister Dammika Patabendi issued a statement today (23) denying that he said elephant Kawanthissa died from diarrhoea. He was responding to a report in a daily Sri Lankan Sinhala-language newspaper that claimed the elephant's death was due to diarrhoea.

The minister said he never made that statement and that no one can decide the cause of death based on personal opinion. He said the cause, whether diarrhoea, a gunshot injury, or another reason, must be found through scientific and medical examinations. The final determination will come from the post-mortem report.

He warned that attributing false statements to him could spread misinformation and create public misconceptions. He asked the newspaper to correct the inaccurate report and share his real position with the public. He said the correction should have the same prominence as the original report.

fce8bbdea9.spoken: Hello and welcome. Environment Minister Dammika Patabendi has spoken out after a newspaper report claimed that the elephant Kawanthissa died because of diarrhoea. The minister says he never said that. In a statement issued today (23), he explained that the real cause of death can only be confirmed by a post-mortem report. He said it could be diarrhoea, a gunshot injury, or something else, but only scientific and medical tests will tell. He is worried that false quotes spread misinformation and confuse the public. So he has asked the newspaper to fix the story and share his actual position with the same importance as the original report. We will wait to see what the post-mortem examination reveals.

9379dc90fd.what_happened: The Sri Lanka Human Rights Commission ordered an investigation into damage allegedly caused to Sigiriya Rock during 2017 conservation work, after a petition by Deeman Ananda. The Commission found drilling, cable installation, and use of modern materials had damaged the rock, and directed several government bodies to take prompt action.
details: The Sri Lanka Human Rights Commission issued a determination on October 20 based on a petition filed by Deeman Ananda. The petition alleged that development and conservation work carried out at the Sigiriya World Heritage site in 2017 had destroyed archaeological evidence, including drilling holes, attaching machinery, altering the Lion’s Paw, and removing ancient inscriptions.

An on-site inspection found a cable system installed from the base to the summit to transport materials, with equipment attached to the rock. The rock had been drilled using electrical equipment, and modern mortar and cement were used in conserving ancient mortar. The Commission said the respondents — the Department of Archaeology, Central Cultural Fund, Ministry of Cultural Affairs, and the Sigiriya Project of the Central Cultural Fund — failed to prove the work had proper approval or followed formal procedure.

The Commission concluded the work caused damage to the rock, the most significant natural and cultural feature of Sigiriya, and warned that development without proper procedures could violate cultural and environmental heritage rights. However, the allegation that ancient inscriptions were removed could not be substantiated; the Department of Archaeology said only seven inscriptions had been identified in the area. The Commission stressed the need for a proper mechanism under joint supervision of the Department of Archaeology, the Cultural Triangle, and the National Building Research Organisation for activities of national importance, and made several recommendations to protect archaeological sites and preserve their historical value.
9379dc90fd.why_it_matters: The Commission warned that development without proper procedures could violate rights relating to cultural and environmental heritage.

9379dc90fd.spoken: Good morning. The Sri Lanka Human Rights Commission has ordered a full investigation into damage done to the iconic Sigiriya Rock. This follows a petition by Deeman Ananda, who said conservation work back in 2017 drilled holes into the rock, attached heavy machinery, and even altered the famous Lion’s Paw. Inspectors confirmed a cable system was run from the base to the summit, and modern cement was used on ancient mortar. The Commission found that the Department of Archaeology, the Central Cultural Fund, and other bodies could not prove the work had proper approval. They concluded the rock — the most significant natural and cultural feature of Sigiriya — was damaged, and warned that such unapproved development violates cultural and environmental heritage rights. The claim that ancient inscriptions were removed couldn’t be proven; only seven inscriptions are known in the area. Now the Commission has directed those agencies to act quickly and set up a joint supervision mechanism with the National Building Research Organisation for any future work of national importance.

8d382feb9c.what_happened: A 16-year-old died after a car went out of control and hit a bus stop on S. de S. Jayasinghe Mawatha in Kohuwala on Monday evening (Nov. 23). The car had been travelling from Nugegoda towards Kohuwala and hit a motorcycle and the rear of another car before striking the child at the bus stop. The child was taken to Colombo South Teaching Hospital in Kalubowila but died, and the 68-year-old driver was arrested.
details: Police said the car was going from Nugegoda towards Kohuwala when it lost control. It first hit a motorcycle and the back of another car. The car then hit the child, who was at a nearby bus stop, before hitting another motorcycle, a car and a van.

The child was seriously injured and was admitted to the Colombo South Teaching Hospital in Kalubowila. The child later died from the injuries. Three other people hurt in the accident were also admitted to the hospital.
The dead child was a resident of the Nugegoda area. The car driver, aged 68, is a resident of Morawila in Panadura and has been arrested. Kohuwala Police are carrying out further investigations.

7065e31ab1.what_happened: Sri Lanka inaugurated its first comprehensive national battery testing centre, the Centre for E-Mobility and Battery Technology, on Monday (Nov. 23) at the National Engineering Research and Development Centre. The facility was established under the patronage of Minister of Science and Technology Prof. Chrishantha Abeysena.
details: Sri Lanka opened its first comprehensive national battery testing centre, the Centre for E-Mobility and Battery Technology, at the National Engineering Research and Development Centre on Monday (Nov. 23). The inauguration was held under the patronage of Minister of Science and Technology Prof. Chrishantha Abeysena. Attendees included Ministry Secretary Dr. Roshanie Dissanayake, NERDC Chairman Dr. Chithral Ambawatte, Acting Director General Manoj Karunaratne and representatives of local and international industries.

The facility was established with a total investment of approximately Rs. 161.5 million, comprising Rs. 118 million from the Government's National Quality Infrastructure Strengthening Project and Rs. 43.5 million contributed by NERDC. It can assess battery performance, capacity, durability and safety under different environmental conditions, and also tests electric vehicle charging equipment and various battery systems.

The centre aims to expand Sri Lanka’s battery testing capabilities beyond conventional assessments to include modern battery technologies, supporting the development of electric mobility and renewable energy sectors. It will provide specialised testing services to local manufacturers, importers, researchers and technology developers, while supporting domestic product development and increasing local value addition.
7065e31ab1.why_it_matters: Expands battery testing to support Sri Lanka's electric mobility and renewable energy sectors.

d932426328.what_happened: Fisheries Minister Ramalingam Chandrasegar has ordered an urgent investigation into mass fish deaths at Kilinochchi Tank. The directive followed a telephone discussion with Northern Province Governor Nagalingam Vedanayagam. Fish, freshwater prawns and juvenile fish reportedly died in the lower section of the tank.
details: Fisheries Minister Ramalingam Chandrasegar ordered an urgent probe after large numbers of fish, freshwater prawns and juvenile fish died in the lower part of Kilinochchi Tank. He issued the directive after speaking by telephone with Northern Province Governor Nagalingam Vedanayagam. The minister also called for a report on the incident.

Concerns have been raised over water-release procedures and possible problems during irrigation operations. Chandrasegar requested an assessment of financial losses suffered by freshwater fishing families who lost fish stocks and fishing equipment. An environmental assessment was also ordered to determine the impact on water quality and the surrounding ecosystem.
The minister said the causes of the fish deaths must be identified. He called for appropriate measures to provide relief to affected fishing communities.

d932426328.spoken: Hello and welcome. Fisheries Minister Ramalingam Chandrasegar has ordered an urgent investigation after large numbers of fish, freshwater prawns and juvenile fish died in the lower section of Kilinochchi Tank. The minister made the decision after a telephone call with Northern Province Governor Nagalingam Vedanayagam. Authorities are worried about water-release procedures and possible issues during irrigation operations. The minister also wants an assessment of money lost by fishing families whose stocks and equipment were destroyed, plus an environmental check on water quality and the surrounding ecosystem. He has asked for the causes to be found and for relief to be provided to affected communities. A report on the incident has been requested. This is a developing story from Sri Lanka's Northern Province.

61ab9a2065.what_happened: The World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called for the lifting of a US fuel blockade on Cuba. He warned that the sanctions were endangering the lives of children. He visited Cuba and toured healthcare facilities in Havana.
details: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus is the World Health Organization chief. He called for the lifting of a US fuel blockade on Cuba. He warned that the sanctions were endangering the lives of children during a Tuesday visit to Cuba that included tours of several healthcare facilities in Havana.

During his three-day visit, his organisation would contribute $2m to help strengthen Cuba’s national immunisation programme and provide essential medical equipment to healthcare facilities. The UN has repeatedly warned of a growing humanitarian crisis on the island and called the US blockade a violation of international law and the human rights of all Cubans. Tedros said the intensification of fuel restrictions and sanctions was causing direct harm to the Cuban people, especially the most vulnerable.

Cuba’s government says the measures led to daily power outages lasting 20 hours or more, critical shortages of medicines and surgical supplies, and a decline in health indicators, such as infant mortality rates. Tedros met with Cuba’s President Miguel Diaz-Canel on Tuesday and they agreed on the need to prioritise essential health services and time-sensitive interventions, particularly for children, Tedros wrote in a post on X. Tedros said fuel restrictions and sanctions affecting the purchase of medical products were severely impacting the health system that Cuban doctors had built over decades.

Tedros said during a news conference that Cuba’s life expectancy had fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 years in 2025, the first decline since records began in 1950, and the 2025 figures predate the imposition by the administration of US President Donald Trump of a fuel blockade and stiff sanctions against a number of Cuban officials and entities in January. Washington argues the energy blockade is intended to push for political change on the island and says that exports of food and medicine are subject to legal exemptions. An annual non-binding resolution calling for an end to a US embargo on the island has passed in favour of Cuba in the UN General Assembly by wide margins every year since 1992.
